messages:
incidents-bot: ALERT: p99 spike detected for /v1/stream (prod) across us-west-2 + eu-west-1. p95 -> 780ms (baseline ~120ms), p99 -> 3.2s (baseline ~420ms). streaming stall rate 29%. Paging oncall-eng. :rotating_light:
maya: I'm oncall, ack. pulling up dashboards and logs now.
tom: oncall SRE here, joining. any deploys in the last 20m?
li: saw a config push ~12m ago to kvcache eviction policy from sam's change list. also KV cache miss-rate jumped 3x for streaming keyspace.
sam: rolled eviction change to reduce mem pressure — only targeted warm pools. I didn't expect wide misses. rolling back if that's the cause.
maya: quick checks:
```
# pod state
kubectl get pods -n inference -l role=batcher -o wide
# check pending pods and events
kubectl get events -n inference --sort-by='.lastTimestamp' | tail -n 30
# tail error counts
kubectl logs -n inference deploy/stream-router -c router | grep -i "stall\|timeout" | wc -l
```
ops-bot: autoscaler note: replica autoscale throttled - unable to provision GPU nodes in us-west-2a for last 4m (quota exhausted). Pending pods: 3.
maya: that explains partial underprovisioning + cache miss storm = tail queues.
tom: can we immediately shift a subset of traffic to fallback-small model variant and route new sessions away from affected batchers? runbook: RouteShift -> fallback-small.
elaine: CS reporting 3 enterprise customers experiencing stream freezes. CS notified and sending status.
sam: rolling back eviction flag now — pushing config revert to config-service (canary first).
```
# revert config
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/revert -d '{"service":"kvcache","key":"eviction-policy","to":"previous"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $REVERT_TOKEN"
```
sam: revert pushed to canary (2 pods), monitoring.
li: metrics: after revert to canary can see cache-hit rate improving in canary pods (hit-rate +12%). overall cluster still bad because routing heavy to affected AZ.
maya: manual mitigations executed: 1) kubectl scale deployment/batcher-3 -n inference --replicas=8 2) enabled route-shift for 20% traffic to fallback-small 3) temporarily disabled batcher adaptive batching (to reduce head-of-line)
```
kubectl scale deploy/batcher-3 -n inference --replicas=8
curl -X POST https://router-api.redwood.internal/route-shift -d '{"route":"/v1/stream","variant":"fallback-small","percent":20}'
# disable adaptive batching
curl -X POST https://config.redwood.internal/api/v1/patch -d '{"service":"batcher","key":"adaptive_batching","value":false}'
```
tom: also requested GPU quota increase from infra team for us-west-2; response ETA 12m.
ops-bot: infra request logged as INFRA-7845, ETA 10-15m.
maya: quick log check after actions: grep for 'stall' dropped from 540 -> 78 in the last 3m. p95 now ~320ms, p99 ~1.1s in us-west. still elevated but improving.
li: streaming stall rate down to 8% cluster-wide. eu-west still at 14% (routing lag).
sam: can confirm full revert will be promoted to all regions in 4m if canary stays green. plan: promote after 10m stable.
elaine: CS update sent: short blip, mitigations applied, next update in 30m. customers asked to escalate if they see further stalls.
maya: creating incident ticket INC-18321, tagging "latency/streaming/tail" and assigning to SRE.
tom: I'll take 1h watch. maya handing off now — please escalate to lucy (next oncall) if metrics worsen or if p99 > 2s again.
maya: handoff notes: what happened = kvcache eviction change increased miss-rate; compounding factor = autoscaler couldn't add GPU nodes in us-west-2a (quota). mitigations = revert eviction flag, manual scale, route-shift to fallback model, disable adaptive batching. followups: infra quota review, add automated quota health to paging rule, add canary guard for kvcache policy changes.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-18321 link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-18321.
tom: monitoring dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/streaming/stream-latency?orgId=1&from=-30m&to=now
li: quick checklist for postmortem: timing of config push, autoscaler scaling events, quota failure timeline, affected tenant list, customer impact window.
maya: thanks all. I'll join the postmortem if needed. logging final: p95 ~200ms, p99 ~470ms, stall rate ~2% cluster-wide at handoff.
elaine: CS will follow up with customers; file for credits if SLA breach confirmed. :white_check_mark:
tom: taking watch, will update every 10m or on regression.
maya: handing off. :wave:
